title: Dial.1 rem early: hard Scripture paths; learn from the saints
english: A presses Hermias: at home in quiet, does he keep the divine word in mind, holy books in hand, eagerness sharpening the mind like keen-nosed hounds for the hunt of what must be learned — or will old age be blamed for slackness? Hermias answers that the body is weak at life’s evening, yet the mind still loves learning; like a noble colt forced onto rough, unbroken ground, zeal for the God-breathed Scripture meets paths hard to enter and hard to tread, and at times the rough country drives the mind toward hesitation — especially when the talk is about the faith, the chief point of our hope.

A agrees: gifts from above are not won without sweat. Things too high, with a glory set apart, are not easy trails for whoever wants them; they are hard to take, hard to enter, uphill. What then should those do who long for these fairest findings when reaching them is hardest? Nothing else, A says, than to trust the ways of the holy ones.

title: Dial.1 rem mid: Horeb mediator type; the prophet like Moses; Son speaks the Father’s words
english: From Deuteronomy at Horeb on the day of the assembly Israel asked not to hear the Lord’s voice or see the great fire again, lest they die. The Lord said they spoke rightly, and promised: [[I will raise up a prophet for them from among their brothers, like you >> Bible:Deuteronomy 18:18]], and put my word in his mouth. In Moses’ shadows, A argues, human weakness already showed how needed a mediator is.

Israel said to Moses, [[You speak to us… and let not God speak to us, lest we die >> Bible:Exodus 20:19]]. The Creator accepted that request and, shaping the truth beforehand in types, promised Christ’s mediation. The Son himself cries, [[I have not spoken from myself; the Father who sent me has given me commandment what to say >> Bible:John 12:49]], and [[the words I speak are not mine but his who sent me >> Bible:John 14:24]]. John seals it: the one God sent speaks the words of God. Hermias will not deny the point; A offers to stay on this path of the Son’s mediation rather than dart down another road.

title: Dial.1 rem CLOSEOUT: Father and Son names mark begetting, not interchangeable ranks
english: Truth — that is, Christ — does not lie when he says to the Father, [[All that is mine is yours, and yours mine, and I am glorified in them >> Bible:John 17:10]]. If “Father” and “Son” were only titles of rank like other shared honors, what would stop us from erasing the difference and calling both Fathers and Sons, crowned alike? Hermias finds that wholly unbelievable: the Father remains Father; the Son remains Son and is not thought Father.

A: most true. So fatherhood’s name on the Father is not a mere badge of dignity, nor sonship’s name on the Son, as when both are called life or light; each name is proper and shows how each is. To refuse pouring the names into one another, and to ask a stable seat for each, keeps each one’s being unaltered: the Father is Father and not Son, because he has begotten; the Son is Son and not Father, because he has been begotten. Strip the names in thought and call each simply God or life or king — the distinction goes dark. Only by thinking “he has begotten” is the Father truly marked; only by being thought begotten is the Son. That closes Dialogue 1’s rem path. DIALOGUE 1 CLOSEOUT.
